answer: Make the tenth clone cost more than the first. Each identity posts a stake that thickens as copies appear: the schedule is a dune, collateral rising with every new key clustering near an existing one, so n clones pay convexly more, never one deposit split n ways. Attestation weight flows only from quorums across distinct clusters. Every key carries a ferrous hardware tag bound at issuance; moving it slashes the cluster. Like a cedar adding one ring per epoch, fresh identities gain weight slowly: a botnet ages no faster than one honest agent. Attacker cost tracks headcount.
